content:
As the number of Mac AI agents requesting "full disk access" permissions surges, Apple says it will adjust macOS to protect user privacy.

Although Apple has not disclosed specific details, the company said users should understand the real implications of granting such "extremely high" permissions to applications.

In a blog post on its Developer website, Apple explained that the full disk access feature in macOS was originally designed to "allow backup applications to function properly on Mac." However, Apple noted that "some developers" have been using macOS full disk access in ways that could put users at risk.

In response, Apple said it would "introduce additional control features to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant such extremely high permissions to applications must do so through very deliberate user actions."

The company did not elaborate further on these control measures or the planned changes. However, Apple said that the rise of AI agents with "increasingly powerful capabilities and autonomy" is raising significant privacy and security concerns:

Apple's statement comes as tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots are gaining popularity. These long-running AI agents require access to large amounts of personal user data, and we have already witnessed several negative incidents involving Meta Muse.
